description: Simplified RFI (open-raise-first-in) ranges by position, 9-handed live $1/$2-$2/$3. Source: docs/research/01-preflop-strategy.md.

actions.combos: 77+, A7s+, A5s, KJs+, QJs, JTs, AJo+

rationale_parts.lead: From UTG (first to act), open only a tight, strong range: 77+, big suited aces, KJs+, QJs, JTs and AJo+ at 3bb.
points: With 7–8 players still to act behind you, someone often has a real hand — only strong pairs, big suited aces and the best Broadways survive that much traffic.
Offsuit Broadways like KJo and the small pairs stay out: they get dominated (beaten by similar-but-better hands) or have to fold too often when the table fights back.

actions.combos: 66+, A7s+, A5s, KTs+, QTs+, JTs, T9s, AJo+

rationale_parts.lead: From UTG+1, open just slightly wider than UTG — add 66, KTs/QTs and connectors down to T9s — still at 3bb.
points: One fewer player behind you means 66's set-mining odds and the suited connectors' straight/flush chances now just clear the bar.
It's still an early seat: no offsuit KQ, no pairs below 66 — a raise here still runs into 6–7 possible wake-ups and gets dominated too often when called.

actions.combos: 66+, A7s+, A5s, KTs+, QTs+, JTs, T9s, 98s, AJo+, KQo

rationale_parts.lead: UTG+2 is the bridge from early to middle position: add 98s and KQo — the first offsuit Broadway — and keep everything else early-position tight.
points: With 5–6 players left to act, KQo's top-pair value and blockers now outweigh its domination risk.
The pair floor stays at 66: small pairs still don't get the right price to set-mine (call hoping to flop three of a kind) with this many players behind.

actions.combos: 66+, A5s+, KTs+, QTs+, JTs, T9s, 98s, AJo+, KQo

rationale_parts.lead: From the lojack, open 66+, suited aces, suited Broadways, connectors down to 98s, plus AJo+ and KQo at 3bb.
points: Only 4–5 players remain behind, so the medium pairs gain implied odds (bigger payoffs when they hit) and KQo holds up — fewer players can wake up with a monster.

actions.combos: 55+, A4s+, KTs+, QTs+, J9s+, T9s, 98s, ATo+, KJo+

rationale_parts.lead: From the hijack, extend the range down to 55 and add suited connectors from J9s, opening at 2.5bb.
points: A shorter field means fewer multiway pots, so the drawing hands can actually realize their straight and flush potential instead of getting squeezed out.

rationale_parts.lead: From the cutoff, open wide: any pair, suited connectors down to 65s, and offsuit Broadways like QTo/JTo at 2.5bb.
points: Only 2–3 players act after you, so set-mining pays with any pair.
The offsuit Broadways can now steal the blinds outright and dominate the weaker hands that call them.

rationale_parts.lead: On the button, open the widest range at the table — any pair, weak suited aces, suited connectors down to 54s, and offsuit hands down to K9o/T9o at 2.5bb.
points: Only the two blinds are left, and you're guaranteed position (acting last) on every street — that edge turns marginal cards into profitable opens.
Most of these hands still fold to a 3-bet (a re-raise); the profit comes from stealing blinds and outplaying the blinds after the flop.

rationale_parts.lead: From the small blind it's raise or fold: open pairs, suited aces, suited Broadways and connectors at 3bb, and don't limp.
points: You act last before the flop but FIRST on every street after it, so only hands with real showdown value justify playing the whole hand out of position.
Marginal offsuit hands need position to be worth playing — fold them rather than limp into a bad spot.
